No more delayed PDL release: Remulla justifies proposed transfer of BJMP to DOJ. The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) ought to be transferred to the Department of Justice (DOJ), if only to avoid delays in the release of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) due to messy paperwork. Thus, said DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla during the agency’s marathon budget hearing before the House Committee on Appropriations Thursday, Aug. 27. It was Makabayan lawmaker ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio who raised the unfortunate issue of inmates being kept in BJMP custody because of the clerical matter. Remulla responded by saying that it would be better to transfer the BJMP to the DOJ since the latter handles the records of PDLs. “It is our position that the BJMP should be transferred under the [DOJ], under the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor),” he told Tinio, a deputy minority leader. “Dalawang pong karpeta eh, may karpeta ang BJMP, may karpeta ang Bucor," noted the DILG chief (There are two folders, the BJMP has its own folder, and the BuCor has its own folder). "I think it would be prudent for Congress to help us into combining the BuCor and BJMP into one facility since they perform the same jobs, basically, they just mirroring each other,” he reckoned. Aside from the BJMP, Remulla also proposed transferring to the DOJ municipal and provincial jails. “So we’re asking Congress for help, the President’s help, in combining the two agencies for more efficient use of resources and for fair treatment of the Persons Deprived of Liberty if they have to release of not,” Remulla said. Under the present system, inmates or PDLs are detained in municipal, city, and provincial jails while their cases are being heard. Once sentenced, they are transferred to the New Bilibid Prison (NBP), which is managed by the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) under the DOJ. Located in Muntinlupa City, the NBP has a population of over 20,000, which is nearly 200 percent above its intended capacity.

School bag yields marijuana, 8 live bullets; student arrested in Tuguegarao. TUGUEGARAO CITY — A routine security check at a private school here led to the arrest of a 20-year-old college student after suspected marijuana and eight live 9mm rounds were allegedly found in his backpack on Monday, August 24. Police said the student, identified only as alias “Mar,” a resident of Barangay Ngarag, Cabagan, Isabela, was stopped for inspection at about 11:56 a.m. at the school’s pedestrian entrance along Balzain Highway in Barangay Centro 12. A female security officer conducting the routine bag inspection reportedly discovered two pieces of suspected marijuana weighing 1.78 grams and valued at about P213. A glass tube reportedly containing marijuana residue and eight live 9mm ammunition were also found inside the backpack. The discovery prompted the security officer to alert authorities, resulting in the student’s arrest and turnover to the Tuguegarao City Police Station. Police said the confiscated items would be turned over to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 2 for examination and proper disposition. The student is facing charges under Sections 11 and 12 of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, for alleged possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia. He is also facing a charge under Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Law on Firearms and Ammunition, for alleged illegal possession of the eight live rounds. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the source and intended use of the ammunition and suspected illegal drugs.

College student killed, girlfriend wounded in Ilocos Norte shooting. NUEVA ERA, Ilocos Norte — A 24-year-old college student was killed while his girlfriend was wounded when they were shot by a motorcycle-riding gunman in front of their residence in Barangay Uguis here Thursday night, August 27. Police identified the fatality as alias "Jay,” a resident of Sitio Tres, Barangay Uguis. His girlfriend, also a college student, and a resident of Burgos, Ilocos Norte, suffered gunshot wounds in the leg and abdomen. Police said the victims had just arrived home at around 7:30 p.m. when a 19-year-old suspect, a resident of the same barangay, allegedly approached them on a motorcycle and fired four shots from a still unknown firearm Jay sustained multiple gunshot wounds. He and his girlfriend were rushed to a hospital in Sinait, Ilocos Sur, but he was declared dead upon arrival. The suspect is now the subject of a hot-pursuit operation. The Nueva Era police are continuing their investigation and awaiting the SOCO findings.

DSWD, DDB pilot program to curb drug abuse risks among street children, out-of-school youth. Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and psychosocial support. The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), in partnership with the Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB), is piloting “Program Silong,” an integrated program to be implemented through Special Drug Education Centers (SDECs). The agencies conducted a week-long training for the program’s pilot implementation from Aug. 24 to 28 in Quezon City. DSWD Special Assistant to the Secretary for Innovations Helen Suzara said the initiative seeks to strengthen drug and substance abuse prevention efforts among children and young people. “Silong is an important step in strengthening our collective efforts towards drug abuse prevention, particularly among children and the young people,” Suzara said during the opening of the training. The program has four components covering drug abuse prevention education, family involvement and support, community mobilization, and psychosocial and auxiliary services. The education component includes toolkits designed for children, early to late adolescents, and parents or caregivers. The family component will provide interventions to help parents and caregivers support drug abuse prevention efforts, while the community component will encourage communities to develop and implement prevention activities. The psychosocial component will use pre- and post-assessments to identify the needs of children in street situations and out-of-school youth and monitor their progress. Suzara described Program Silong as “a pioneering initiative, the first of its kind in the Philippines and in the ASEAN region.” The program will initially be piloted in Muntinlupa City, Occidental Mindoro, and Zamboanga del Sur. DSWD said the initiative is in line with its mandate under the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, to provide drug abuse prevention and developmental services to vulnerable children and youth. It will also involve community volunteers and local government implementers in carrying out prevention activities in the pilot areas.

No place for violence, bullying in Baguio - Mayor Magalong. BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City. This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he assured that the two separate violent incidents involving high school students are now being handled by the Baguio City Police Office. Magalong urged the public not to circulate a video involving one of the cases to prevent online abuse. "While we do not condone these acts among the youth, we should also respect the dignity, privacy, and well-being of the children involved." He asked the public not to "share, repost, or further circulate the video" as further dissemination could expose minors to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse. Magalong urged the public to allow police authorities, school officials, and social workers to address the two separate cases judiciously. “Let us not amplify violence. Let us protect our children and help build a safer, kinder, and more respectful Baguio,” he said. The police said the two cases are being handled separately with details treated confidentially because minors are involved. The first incident involving students reportedly occurred outside the school premises of a high school at around 3 p.m. on August 26. Investigation report said complaints were filed with Police Station 2 and the minors involved, described as Grade 9 and Grade 10 students, have been identified. Personnel of the Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) coordinated with the school authorities while appropriate intervention was undertaken with the assistance of social workers. Police Station 2 had scheduled another coordination meeting on August 28 to discuss the matter and the appropriate interventions. The second incident reportedly involved Grade 7 and Grade 9 students from another secondary school and was reported to Police Station 5 at around 1 p.m. on August 27. The incident allegedly happened during recess on August 24 inside a classroom causing an injury to the complainant. Police said WCPD personnel coordinated with the school principal and class advisers and a dialogue was later held with the students and their parents or guardians with administrative sanctions expected to be imposed.

It works! Lucena inventor creates trash-collecting robot from recycled materials. LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city. The device was constructed using old plastic containers, aluminum, and galvanized wire mesh. It is equipped with a garbage lifter designed to easily gather and collect floating debris. The robot is operated via a remote control—similar to those used in computer games—that controls a small motor attached to the unit. According to Isagani Inciong, an electronics technician and the device's inventor, he conceived the project to help reduce floating river debris, particularly plastic waste. Tests conducted at the Iyam River proved the robot effective at gathering and retrieving floating trash. Inciong added that aside from being fun to operate, the robot offers significant environmental benefits. He believes that if more people use or "play" with this type of robot, a larger volume of waste can be recovered from waterways. He also called on local government units (LGUs) to take notice of his invention and expressed willingness to collaborate with authorities to refine the design and build a larger version of the robot to support more extensive river rehabilitation efforts.

Philippine exports, imports lose steam as second half begins. Philippine merchandise trade lost momentum at the start of the second half of 2026, as both exports and imports posted slower annual growth in July and fell in value from the previous month. The latest preliminary Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data released on Friday, Aug. 28, showed exports grew by 10.8 percent year-on-year to $8.15 billion in July, sharply slower than the 25-percent expansion in June. Imports likewise rose by 19.8 percent to $14.12 billion, easing from the 25-percent growth recorded a month ago. In value terms, exports fell by $681.31 million, or 7.7 percent, from the revised monthly record high of $8.83 billion in June, while imports declined by $204.52 million, or 1.4 percent, from $14.33 billion. As a result, total external trade dropped by $885.83 million, or 3.8 percent, month-on-month to $22.27 billion from $23.16 billion. The July export value was the lowest since May, when outbound shipments amounted to $7.95 billion, while imports were also at their lowest since May’s $14.05 billion. The slower trade performance came despite continued strong demand for Philippine electronic products, which remained the country’s top export commodity. Electronics exports reached $4.79 billion in July, accounting for 58.8 percent of total outbound shipments. They also recorded the biggest annual increase among commodity groups, rising by $869.72 million from $3.92 billion a year ago. Other commodities that contributed to the annual increase in exports were gold, which rose by $79.34 million; electronic equipment and parts, up by $71.81 million; machinery and transport equipment, up by $50.06 million; and woodcrafts and furniture, up by $30.92 million. By major type of goods, manufactured goods remained the largest source of export earnings at $6.61 billion, equivalent to 81.1 percent of total. Mineral products followed at $776.61 million, or 9.5 percent of total, while agro-based products accounted for $548.95 million, or 6.7 percent. Despite the July slowdown, exports in the first seven months of the year climbed by 12.9 percent to $54.92 billion from $48.67 billion in the same period last year, the highest January-to-July export value since the series began in 1991. The United States (US) remained the Philippines’ biggest export market in July, accounting for $1.68 billion, or 20.7 percent of total exports. It was followed by Hong Kong at $1.29 billion, China at $919.82 million, Japan at $856.6 million, and Singapore at $401.17 million. On the import side, electronic products also posted the biggest annual increase, surging by $1.75 billion to $4.6 billion and accounting for 32.6 percent of total imports. This was followed by mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials, which increased by $502.71 million to $1.95 billion, and cereals and cereal preparations, which rose by $187.36 million to $561.06 million. Raw materials and intermediate goods comprised the biggest share of imports at $5.71 billion, or 40.4 percent, followed by capital goods at $3.84 billion, or 27.2 percent, and consumer goods at $2.58 billion, or 18.3 percent. From January to July, imports increased by 18.9 percent to $92.26 billion from $77.58 billion a year ago, also the highest first-seven-month import value since the series began in 1991. China remained the country’s largest source of imported goods, supplying $4.17 billion, or 29.5 percent of total imports in July. It was followed by South Korea with $1.8 billion, Japan with $1.11 billion, Indonesia with $807.75 million, and the US with $766.61 million. With imports continuing to outpace exports, the country’s balance of trade in goods posted a deficit of $5.97 billion in July, 34.9 percent wider than the $4.43-billion shortfall a year ago and the widest since the $6.1-billion deficit recorded in May. Total external trade nevertheless remained 16.3 percent higher than the $19.14 billion recorded in July last year, although its annual growth also slowed from 25 percent in June. Imports accounted for 63.4 percent of July trade, while exports comprised the remaining 36.6 percent. - with a report from Danielle T. Bayani

Japanese Ambassador Endo bids farewell, thanks Filipinos for support and friendship. Outgoing Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya bade farewell to Filipinos on Friday, Aug. 28, as he ended his two-and-a-half-year tour of duty, describing his time in the country as "truly unforgettable." In an X post, Endo thanked Filipinos for their "unwavering" support and friendship, saying he was deeply humbled to have served as ambassador "at the height of our two countries’ partnership." "Taos-pusong pasasalamat, Pilipinas (My sincerest thanks, Philippines)!” he wrote. “These two and a half years have been truly unforgettable, and I am deeply humbled to have served as Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines at the height of our two countries’ partnership," he added. In a video accompanying the post, Endo also thanked Filipinos for their friendship and support. "Maraming salamat sa walang humpay ninyong suporta at pagkakaibigan (Thank you very much for your unwavering support and friendship),” he said. “Hanggang sa muli! Mata ne (Until we meet again. See you)!” he added. Endo’s farewell message came a day after President Marcos honored him during a farewell call at Malacañang, where the President conferred on him the Order of Sikatuna, Grand Cross with Distinction, for his contributions to strengthening Philippine-Japan relations. According to the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), Endo was recognized for promoting bilateral exchanges and deepening cooperation in defense, security, and development cooperation, as well as supporting Philippine priorities in infrastructure, education, transportation, maritime domain awareness, and human resource development. The PCO also cited Endo's efforts to advance Japan's longstanding commitment to peace and development in Mindanao, including support for the peace process, grassroots development, and the transition of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao. The award likewise recognized his efforts to mobilize Japanese humanitarian and development assistance during natural disasters and recent regional crises, as well as initiatives that fostered friendship, mutual understanding, and goodwill between Filipinos and Japanese. The Order of Sikatuna is conferred on individuals who have rendered exceptional and meritorious service to the Philippines or made outstanding contributions to Philippine-Japan relations. The Philippines and Japan are marking 70 years of normalized relations this year, with 15 years of Strengthened Strategic Partnership since 2011, and bilateral ties having expanded across economic, development, security, and people-to-people cooperation.

Muntinlupa’s Doctor of Medicine Program now CHED-certified. The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has awarded a Certificate of Program Compliance (COPC) to the Doctor of Medicine program in Muntinlupa. The program is offered by the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Muntinlupa (PLMun)–Ospital ng Muntinlupa (OsMun) College of Medicine. “We can now say that our very own PLMun–OsMun College of Medicine fully meets CHED’s official policies, standards, and guidelines,” said Muntinlupa Mayor Ruffy Biazon. Under Joint CHED–Professional Regulation Commission Circular No. 1 issued in 2025, the PRC will not admit applicants for licensure exams from state and local universities and colleges without COPC or government recognition. PLMun, funded by the city government, is the first local university in the country to offer a Doctor of Medicine program among 140 local colleges and universities. With the granting of the COPC, the Muntinlupa City government said CHED has confirmed that the program meets standards, including qualified faculty, adequate resources, and suitable facilities for medical education. “Isa ulit itong milestone (This is another milestone) towards our goal of producing more homegrown healthcare professionals,” the mayor added. Last July, the first batch of PLMun–OsMun College of Medicine graduates completed their studies and are now undergoing internship at OsMun. The graduates are Princess Garcia, Aileen Mae Arban, Maxine Barlaw, Tricia Guevarra, Sophia Laranan, Ana Marie Ramos, and Jaycee Mae Rufino.

Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation donates 1,000 sacks of rice to Baguio, Benguet LGUs. BAGUIO CITY – The Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation distributed 1,000 sacks of 5 kilos of rice to three local government units for residents affected by the previous typhoon and the southwest monsoon. The donation, spearheaded by the Federation of Filipino Chinese Chambers of Commerce & Industry, Inc.-Baguio Chapter led by Peter Ng, together with its members, delivered 300 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) to the Benguet provincial government, on August 27, which were received by Governor Melchor Diclas. Diclas expressed his deep gratitude to the Baguio Filipino-Chinese community for its continuing support, particularly during times of calamity. In the capital town of La Trinidad, officials also received 200 sacks (5 kilos each) of rice provided by the group for the disaster victims. Another 500 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) were personally delivered by Ng and his group to the Office of the City Social Welfare and Development Office in Baguio City, which were received by City Administrator Vittorio Jericho Cawis and OCWD Officer Liza Balungayan. “On behalf of Mayor Benjamin Magalong, thank you very much for the tireless support to the city government of the Filipino-Chinese community, not only during the disaster, but also for their continued support for the city’s tourism development programs,” said Cawis. He said that based on ODSWDO data, more than 1,000 families were severely affected by the southwest monsoon. It can be recalled that last year, the foundation also donated 1,000 bags of five kilos of rice to these LGUs to be distributed to those affected by the typhoon. “In our groups, and with the support of the foundation, this is our traditional work to deliver aid to disaster victims. On these occasions, we want to show that we are Filipinos who will continue to help the community,” said Ng.

PH batters bow to Venezuela, miss World Cup final berth. The Philippines missed a chance to qualify in the finals of next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup after falling short against Venezuela, 0-10, in the final match of its group stage in Tainan, Taiwan on Thursday, Aug. 29. A few hours after absorbing a painful 2-8 defeat at the hands of host Chinese Taipei, the Nationals continued their struggle against the more experienced Venezuelans to finish the group stage with a 2-3 win-loss record. They finished fourth behind unbeaten Japan (5-0), Venezuela (4-1) and Chinese Taipei (3-2), who claimed the top 3 slots allocated for next year’s finals in Rockford, Illinois. The three qualified teams joined the United States, Australia and Canada, who clinched spots by finishing in the top 3 of their group stage held in Rockford last July. Despite falling short of their goal, the Nationals still showed promise with victories over world No. 7 Cuba, 6-0, and Great Britain, 6-2, last Wednesday, Aug. 26. They also lost to Japan, 0-3, and Cuba, 0-6.

Work, classes suspended in NCR, 16 provinces starting 1 p.m. on Aug. 28. Work in government offices and classes at all levels in public and private schools in the National Capital Region (NCR) and 16 provinces was suspended starting 1 p.m. Friday, Aug. 28, due to the expected further enhancement of the Southwest Monsoon by a low-pressure area that has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility. The suspension was ordered under Memorandum Circular No. 132 issued by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC). The areas covered are NCR, Abra, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Bataan, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac, Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, Rizal, Oriental Mindoro, and Occidental Mindoro. Government agencies involved in the delivery of basic and health services, disaster preparedness and response, and other vital services will continue their operations despite the suspension. The circular said these agencies must continue rendering the necessary services during the period covered by the suspension. Local chief executives may also implement localized cancellation or suspension of classes and/or work in government offices in other areas, pursuant to relevant laws, rules, and regulations. The suspension of work or adoption of alternative work arrangements in the private sector will be left to management's discretion. The suspension comes as authorities anticipate further strengthening of the Southwest Monsoon due to the low-pressure area that has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility.

Turning 'flood control' to 'flood management'. The UP Resilience Institute-NOAH Center believe that it is important to predict floods. You may ask, why make such predictions when most Filipinos already know where it floods? Why not just focus on making solutions? According to the institute, prediction is understanding the problem. If solutions are applied without fully understanding the problem, it is possible the said problems will be underestimated, and the solutions produced are not suited in handling the problem. With the P1 billion allocation, the UP Resilience Institute-NOAH Center will strengthen the country’s capacity to generate, manage, communicate, and apply scientific information for disaster risk reduction, flood management, environmental protection, and climate resilience. The allocation builds on existing accomplishments in hazard mapping, flood intelligence, resilience education, technical assistance, government partnerships, and open access to disaster-risk data and information. Rather than a stand-alone project fund, the budget will expand systems that translate research into practical information for better public investment decisions. This approach recognizes that resilience requires the integration of natural systems, scientific data, and evidence-based governance. The appropriation is consistent with Republic Act No. 9500, or the UP Charter of 2008, which mandates the University to provide scholarly and technical assistance to government, the private sector, and civil society. The funding therefore rests on UP’s legal mandate to advance research, public service, and national development. Areas for Budget Utilization High-resolution mapping of major river basins. UPRI-NOAH will update major river-basin maps using advanced geospatial technologies, producing hazard maps with up to one-by-one-meter pixel resolution. Detailed information on waterways, floodplains, land use, watersheds, infrastructure, and exposed communities will support hazard assessments, land-use planning, and preparedness. Support for Oplan Kontra Baha. In cooperation with the Department of Public Works and Highways, the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, local governments, and the private sector, UPRI-NOAH will integrate watershed science, flood modeling, terrain, infrastructure, and local knowledge to identify appropriate structural and non-structural solutions. Simulation of major detention basins. Simulations will integrate surface and subsurface flow of water to assess storage capacity of detention basins, drainage connectivity, downstream effects, and performance under extreme rainfall and future climate conditions, guiding flood-control planning, operations, maintenance, and investment. LiDAR drone surveys with state colleges and universities. Knowledge co-creation with state colleges and universities will include topographic surveys using LiDAR-equipped drones. There will be capacity building programs to train faculty, researchers, and students, while strengthening regional geospatial and resilience-planning capabilities. Native-tree mapping and tree inventory. Mapping and inventories will document native trees and their environmental value, supporting carbon-credit development, carbon accounting, biodiversity conservation, watershed protection, ecological restoration, urban greening, and flood management. Sediment erosion and delivery assessment. Watershed assessments will estimate soil loss, sediment delivery, and sediment yield using rainfall, soil, topography, land cover, and conservation factors. Results will identify rehabilitation priorities and potential impacts on waterways, detention basins, drainage, and flood-management infrastructure. Mapping hidden waterways and undocumented drainage paths. Identifying buried, altered, diverted, or undocumented waterways will improve flood modeling and guide urban planning, drainage improvement, infrastructure design, restoration, and emergency response. Nature-based solutions. Watershed rehabilitation, wetland and floodplain restoration, urban green spaces, permeable surfaces, and tree planting will complement necessary structural measures while supporting biodiversity, carbon sequestration, water quality, erosion control, and stormwater retention. Artificial Intelligence for Disaster Management. The Institute will harness artificial intelligence and advanced analytics to develop decision-support tools that generate actionable information for land-use and infrastructure planning, environmental management, and risk analysis. These will be integrated and analyzed alongside historical disaster data to identify patterns useful for the assessment of risk. These systems may support identification of vulnerable communities, forecasting, early warning, exposure assessment, and prioritization of interventions. AI-assisted benefit-cost assessment will help decision-makers compare projects and identify interventions that are effective, sustainable, financially justified, and capable of protecting the greatest number of people. Transparency and Accountability Every major expenditure will be connected to a defined program, public purpose, implementation plan, technical outputs, measurable indicators, and monitoring and evaluation. Budget implementation will follow applicable procurement and auditing requirements. The UP System will document and monitor fund disbursements. Building on UPRI-NOAH Accomplishments UPRI-NOAH provides nationwide hazard information covering floods, landslides, storm surges, tsunamis, and coastal hazards. A United Nations Development Programme study found that approximately 59.7 percent of local government units utilize NOAH datasets and analytical tools. The NOAH platform has served more than 3.2 million users, recorded approximately 12.9 million location searches in 2025, and reached as many as 2.3 million engagements in a single day. With the UP Open University, the Institute developed free Basics of Resilience online courses, reaching approximately 117,000 enrollees since program inception and 45,000 finishers over the span of two years. Microcredentials, advanced courses, professional training, master’s programs, and partnerships with state colleges and universities strengthen resilience education and regional technical capacity. Partnerships with government agencies, local governments, universities, and communities support forecasting, risk assessment, drainage and flood studies, and operational flood intelligence. Multidisciplinary Quick Response Teams conduct field investigations, drone mapping, geospatial analysis, and engineering assessments to support disaster response, recovery, and rehabilitation. Looking Ahead UPRI-NOAH will expand the coverage, resolution, accuracy, and usefulness of its services; strengthen public education and graduate programs; develop innovative technologies; and connect research more closely with government planning and investment decisions. Long-term collaboration among universities, government, civil society, industry, international organizations, and communities will combine scientific expertise, local knowledge, sound governance, and public participation. The ₱1 billion allocation will be measured by better information, transparency, evidence-based decisions, effective flood management, and reduced disaster risks and losses. Through innovation, education, partnerships, and public service, UPRI-NOAH will continue to transform scientific knowledge into practical action that protects lives and helps build safer, more resilient, and sustainable communities.

Seven films, seven worlds: A visual feast of what’s coming to CinePanalo 2026. A farmer and his carabao on an unlikely journey to Manila. A romance that reaches into the netherworld. A young boy trying to make sense of growing up. An elderly widower, a kodokushi cleaner and a promise about grief. These are just some of the stories waiting for moviegoers at this year’s CinePanalo, and the newly released posters offer the first visual taste of what’s to come. The posters for the festival’s seven full-length films introduce not only their titles but the different moods and worlds that audiences can expect when the films screen in September. There is magic and adventure in Lawrence Fajardo’s “Beast,” which follows an old farmer and his loyal carabao as they travel to Manila. The poster, designed by writer Jim Flores, hints at the film’s unusual journey and emotional core. Then there’s Carl Joseph E. Papa’s “Patay Gutom,” starring Ian Pangilinan, which takes romance and family drama into supernatural territory. Filipino illustrator and film poster artist Denver Balbaboco gives the film a colorful, playful look that seems appropriate for a story involving the netherworld. Balbaboco recently created the new cover art for The Criterion Collection’s release of Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein.” Mikko Baldoza’s “Stuck On You” goes in another direction, mixing romance, danger and comedy. Its poster, designed by Liam Casimiro, reflects that collision with a bold and energetic visual treatment. Thop Nazareno’s “Apol of My Ai” brings things down to a more intimate, coming-of-age story about a young boy dealing with the complications of growing up. The poster by Jermaine Tulbo brings together the people, relationships and music that shape Apol’s world. Tulbo previously designed the poster for “Olsen’s Day,” one of the entries in the 2025 CinePanalo lineup. In “Wantawsan,” Joseph Abello turns an ordinary errand into what appears to be anything but an ordinary day. Abello also designed the poster, giving the film an offbeat visual personality that matches its comic adventure. The more contemplative side of the lineup comes through in BC Amparado’s “Mono No Aware.” The film follows a Filipino kodokushi cleaner and an elderly widower whose promise to one another leads to a story about grief, family and the fleeting nature of life. Davao-based graphic designer and filmmaker Wowa Medroso created its restrained, evocative poster. Medroso’s debut feature, “Kantil,” premiered at Cinemalaya. Then there’s “Multwoh (Patay na Patay Sa’yo),” written and directed by Rodina Singh, which promises a romance with a rather unusual complication: one of the lovers is dead. Multidisciplinary visual creative EA Rosana designed the poster, blending the haunting, funny and tender elements of the story. Rosana previously worked with Singh on the poster for “Dreamboi” and has also worked on projects involving girl group BINI. Taken together, the seven posters make for quite a visual feast and a useful primer for the films themselves. There’s the strange and surreal, the funny and romantic, the supernatural and the deeply human. If the posters are any indication, this year’s CinePanalo lineup isn’t interested in looking like seven versions of the same movie. The seven filmmakers each received a ₱5 million production grant for their respective films. CinePanalo 2026 runs from Sept. 23 to Oct. 4 at Gateway Cineplex 18, Trinoma, Fairview Terraces, Ayala Malls Feliz, Ayala Malls Circuit, Ayala Malls Manila Bay and Market! Market!

Meta vows to share user data in case Philippine authorities see ‘imminent threat’—Hontiveros. Tech giant Meta has agreed to share user data with Philippine law enforcement authorities, especially when there is an imminent threat of violence, Senator Risa Hontiveros said on Friday, August 28. This comes after Meta’s top Asia-Pacific region policy officers held a roundtable meeting at its headquarters in Singapore to discuss the responsibilities of it platforms—particularly Facebook—on the spread of nihilistic violent extremism (NVE). Hontiveros said she sent representatives to join the Philippine delegation of key government officials to Meta’s meeting. As their meeting was drawing to a close without agreement among the parties, Hontiveros’ camp pushed Meta to commit to sharing subscriber information and traffic data to Philippine authorities when there are indications of imminent attacks, to which the social media giant agreed to. “Now that high-ranking Meta officials themselves have pledged to be more proactive regarding potential threats of violence, action against such threats must be swifter,” Hontiveros said. “This is crucial, especially as we are currently pushing for the Child Online Safety and Protection Act, a priority measure of the government. Meta appears ready to tighten its safeguards, as we have already informed them that the bill is nearing passage,” the senator said. Hontiveros is optimistic the agreement will come to play once Congress pass the Child Online Safety and Protection Act, which builds on the safeguards under Republic Act No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act authored by Hontiveros. “I gave strict instructions to the staff who met with Meta: It must be made clear to them that they cannot profit from Filipinos on Facebook without taking responsibility for the content,” she said. “We will hold them to their word," Hontiveros vowed.

Salmon strengthens partnership with EMCOR, expands access to financing across Visayas and Mindanao. Through this collaboration, over 100 EMCOR stores across the VisMin region are now added to Salmon Finance’s growing network of more than 10,000 partner stores nationwide, bringing reliable and convenient financing closer to more Filipinos. Through the partnership, customers shopping at participating EMCOR stores can now access Salmon Product Loans to purchase appliances, furniture, and gadgets through manageable monthly installments. With this, customers can enjoy flexible payment terms of up to six months with 0% interest, and zero downpayment. Aparejo said the partnership reflects the company’s commitment to bringing more convenience and greater value to its customers. “At EMCOR, we continuously look for ways to improve the shopping experience of our customers and reach more communities across the country,” Aparejo said. “Through our partnership with Salmon Finance, we are able to offer fast and reliable financing solutions that make essential products and motorcycles more accessible to Filipino families.”

Janus Del Prado weighs in on Bea Alonzo-Shirley Kuan issue, suggests NDA for actors and managers. Actor Janus Del Prado has weighed in on the controversy involving Bea Alonzo and her former manager Shirley Kuan, saying the public should hear the actress’s side before making conclusions about their falling-out. Janus shared his thoughts on Facebook as the issue continued to generate discussion following Shirley’s public revelation about the alleged reasons behind her decision to end her professional relationship with Bea. “Before you judge Bea, let’s wait to hear her side of the story first. I’m not dismissing what her former manager claimed just yet, but that’s only one side of the story,” Janus wrote. The actor also raised a bigger issue about the relationship between celebrities and their talent managers, suggesting that both sides should consider signing a non-disclosure agreement, or NDA. For Janus, such an agreement could help protect sensitive information shared during a professional relationship—and provide legal protection if that relationship eventually falls apart. “Actors should really consider having an NDA with their managers, and vice versa, to legally protect both parties’ confidential information and reputations. Para when the sh** hits the fan, everyone involved is legally protected,” he said. Janus’ comments come after Shirley’s revelations about her split from Bea became a talking point online. Shirley has also denied allegations that she interfered in Bea’s relationship with her husband, Vincent Co.

Japanese firms launch AI school for humanoid robots. Narashino, Chiba Pref., Aug. 27 -- A consortium of Japanese companies has launched a data center to train physical artificial intelligence on human tasks for deploying humanoid robots in factories and logistics operations. The facility in Narashino, Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, is operated by J-HRTI, a consortium of five companies, including Tsumura & Co., a maker of Chinese herbal medicine, and Yamazen Corp., a machinery trading company. The partners will pool resources to collect vast amounts of work data and train AI, an undertaking difficult for a single company, to put humanoid robots to practical use in industrial settings. The data center can accommodate up to 40 Chinese-made humanoid robots, with operators stationed there. Wearing virtual reality headsets, the operators control the robots and collect data. The facility also includes areas that replicate actual work environments to test potential applications. J-HRTI aims to deploy the robots for simple tasks such as material transport within fiscal 2026, which ends next March. Shoichi Kumagai, an executive officer at Tsumura, said on Wednesday, "Automation and unmanned operations will be necessary to maintain stable supplies (of products) as falling population makes it increasingly difficult to secure workers."

Iloilo officials thank Marcos administration for distribution of various aid programs. ILOILO CITY—Local officials expressed appreciation to the Marcos administration after Executive Secretary Ralph Recto led distribution of various aid programs earlier this week. “Nagpapasalamat kami sa Pangulo sa mga tulong na ibinigay niya rito sa Iloilo. I’ve been telling our people in the province that we are truly being prioritized,” said Iloilo Governor Arthur “Toto” Defensor Jr. During the August 25 distribution program, Recto assured the people of Iloilo they are part of the social aid programs under the administration of President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. Recto distributed the P200,000 aid for each of the 1,721 barangays in the 42 towns and component city of Passi. As part of the Bawat Bayan Makikinabang for Iloilo, Recto reiterated that it is the first time that each barangay in the country has been given aid directly by Malacañang under the Socio-Civic Projects Fund (SCPF). “We extend our sincere gratitude to the Office of the President and Executive Secretary Ralph Recto for his presence and support,” said Barangay Provincial Federation President Amalia Debuque. Of the P200,000 allocated for each barangay, half of it will be for Presidential Scholars of five graduating college students. In Iloilo province alone, there are more than 8,000 graduating students who are going to be beneficiaries of the P20,000 each aid per barangay. In the town of Pavia, Recto also distributed 10 kilos of rice each to an initial 1,500 family beneficiaries. As part of the Bagong Pilipinas Rice Distribution Program, it will benefit a total of 8,000 families in Pavia with P5 million from the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF). Also present during the ceremonial distribution were 1st District Rep. Janette Loreto-Garin, League of the Municipalities of the Philippines (LMP) Iloilo President Mayor Suzette Mamon, municipal mayors, and barangay officials.

PRU POP Run brings running to the next level. Thirty years calls for 30 kilometers. Pru Life UK is marking three decades in the Philippines with PRU POP (Promise of Protection) Run, highlighted by a special 30K race that challenges runners to go beyond the usual fun-run distances. Set Sunday, Aug. 30, at Ayala Triangle Gardens in Makati, the event will feature five race categories – 3K, 5K, 10K, 21K and the centerpiece 30K. The lineup is designed to accommodate a wide range of participants, from beginners taking their first steps into running to seasoned athletes looking for a demanding new milestone. The 30K is particularly significant because distances of this length are relatively uncommon in local running events. Rather than simply adding another category, Pru Life UK created the race as a physical representation of its 30-year journey in the country – 30 kilometers for 30 years of serving Filipino policyholders and communities. But the company sees the run as more than an anniversary gimmick. It celebrates its long-standing commitment to helping Filipinos build healthier and more secure futures. Pru Life UK Vice President and Head of Brand and Integrated Marketing Communications Kathryn Cajucom said the event reflects the idea that preparing for a stronger future involves more than financial security – it also requires healthier habits, discipline and the willingness to make responsible choices every day. That message gives the 30K a deeper meaning: endurance is not only measured by how far a runner can go, but by the habits built along the way. Through PRU POP Run, Pru Life UK hopes to turn its 30th anniversary into a reminder that securing one's future is itself a long-distance journey – one that requires preparation, resilience and consistency. Each race category caters to different fitness levels. Beginners can kick-start their running journey through the 3K and 5K distances, while more experienced runners can challenge themselves in the 10K and 21K events. Those seeking their next big milestone can take on the exclusive 30K race, a distance rarely featured in local running events. Registration is still open at www.prupoprun.com. As it marks three decades of serving Filipinos, Pru Life UK continues its commitment to being the most trusted partner of every life and protector of every future. Through PRU POP Run, the company reinforces its mission of helping Filipinos build healthy habits, stronger financial futures and lasting well-being – one step at a time. The race categories are structured to welcome every fitness level. Beginners can ease into the lifestyle with the 3K or 5K distance, while seasoned weekend runners can test their stamina in the 10K category. Regular runners and marathon trainees can take on the 21K route or the highly anticipated 30K challenge, a special distance in local running events. Beyond the physical challenge, PRU POP Run serves as a timely call for a more active living. In a digital age, it invites young Filipinos and families to step away from screens, step onto the pavement, and experience the real-world joy of movement, community, and personal achievement.

Death toll rises in Nepal-China border disaster as lake poses new flood threat. KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers were racing to find hundreds of people still missing two days after a catastrophic flash flood struck the Himalayan border between Nepal and China, as the death toll rose Friday and authorities warned that an overflowing lake formed after the disaster could trigger further flooding. Nepal police said Friday morning that the country’s death toll had risen to 469 from 390 a day earlier, while China had not updated its report of just three deaths in Tibet. Together, the two countries have said that more than 1,500 people are missing. Nepali and Chinese authorities warned of further flooding from a lake that formed upstream after Wednesday’s disaster and was already overflowing. They urged people in potentially affected areas to move to safer ground. China’s Ministry of Water Resources said Thursday that the lake held around 2 million cubic meters (70 million cubic feet) of water and was expected to receive another 3 million cubic meters (106 million cubic feet) over the next three days. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported Friday morning that the lake’s barrier was more than 10 kilometers (6 miles) from Gyirong Port, the border crossing with Nepal that was engulfed by mud and floodwater. CCTV said the lake was at an elevation of 2,950 meters (9,680 feet), about 1,000 meters (3,280 feet) above Gyirong Port. Nepal Army said that a team was sent to the border point to inspect the Bhotekoshi River amid the potential of more floods. Thousands of people have been evacuated Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said Friday that 3,253 people had been airlifted by helicopter from the country’s disaster area. Flood survivors, including injured people, were taken to Kathmandu and other locations. Foreigners from multiple countries were among the missing, many of them trekkers and pilgrims. Nepali Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet told The Associated Press that a team had been deployed Friday to the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project near the Nepal-China border following reports that people were trapped inside a tunnel. “It is complicated to find the entry and exit points of the tunnel because everything has been covered by mud,” Basnet said. “Our first priority is rescuing the stranded people.” Videos of the disaster showed floodwaters destroying buildings, bridges and vehicles as people ran in front of the stories-high torrent. In the aftermath, broken concrete lay upended in expanses of brown mud that also caked buildings and buried streets. Families around the world hear the news of missing loved ones Rajan Tamang, a restaurant owner in New York City, said he learned from family in Kathmandu that his mother and sister were among those who died, while many other relatives and friends remained missing. “My family was just waking up, and they didn’t even get any information, and suddenly this flood came. Some of them are missing, some of them lost their life and only a few is alive,” he told The Associated Press after a vigil in New York. U.S. President Donald Trump said the flooding was terrible to see, describing how “strong, well-built buildings were wiped out like they were toothpicks.” Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said the U.S. spoke with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide “anything they want.” Scientists who've studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rocks and melted water swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream.

Okinawa governor race opens; LDP seeks comeback after 12 years. NAHA, Okinawa Pref. (Jiji Press) -- The official campaign period began on Thursday for the Sept. 13 gubernatorial election for Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa. The focus is whether the Liberal Democratic Party will be able to retake the helm of the prefecture after a break of about 12 years. The outcome is likely to affect the administration of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, the party's president. On Thursday, six people filed their candidacies, including LDP-backed Genta Koja, 42, former vice mayor of Naha, Okinawa's capital, and incumbent Governor Denny Tamaki, 66, who seeks a third four-year term. Key election issues include a project to relocate the U.S. Marine Corps' Futenma air station in the Okinawa city of Ginowan to the Henoko coastal district in Nago, another Okinawa city, as well as Okinawa's economic development. Delivering his first campaign speech in Naha, Koja said that high prices and traffic congestion are major problems the prefecture needs to tackle, pledging to "change a stagnant prefectural government into one that moves ahead." Tamaki, speaking in the town of Motobu, stressed: "Everything is for the people of the prefecture and for the future. I will devote myself wholeheartedly to serving the people of the prefecture." Tamaki, who opposes the U.S. base relocation, again receives the backing of the All Okinawa camp, which brings together progressive forces and some conservatives. But the camp has suffered a string of defeats in recent mayoral elections. Tamaki therefore prioritizes unaffiliated voters. He did not seek recommendations from the Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan, the Japanese Communist Party or the Social Democratic Party, all of which are members of the camp. Koja, who accepts the base relocation, is backed by the LDP, the Japan Innovation Party, the Democratic Party for the People, Sanseito and the Conservative Party of Japan. His campaign team expects to gain additional votes from conservatives after Mikio Shimoji, a former lawmaker of the House of Representatives, the lower chamber of the Diet, the country's parliament, concluded a policy agreement with the LDP and scrapped his plan to run. Meanwhile, Koja lacks name recognition. Another concern is that Komeito, which left the LDP-led coalition last year, has limited the scope of its backing to a recommendation from its Okinawa prefectural chapter. The Centrist Reform Alliance, formed by Lower House lawmakers from the CDP and Komeito, has left its members free to vote independently. The base relocation issue has long been central to Okinawa's gubernatorial elections. Tamaki, however, came under criticism after a 17-year-old high school girl died in a March boat accident during a peace education program organized by a group supporting Tamaki. The girl was visiting Henoko on a school trip to see the planned U.S. base relocation site. He plans to emphasize his track record over the past eight years in office, including strong performance of the tourism sector. Koja has pledged to double per capita prefectural income. The other four candidates are company head Shun Kaneshima, 48, medical corporation leader Masahiro Sueyoshi, 73, company representative Takashi Higa, 49, and political group leader Chosuke Yara, 74. The upcoming gubernatorial election, the 15th of its kind since Okinawa's reversion to Japan in 1972, has the largest number of candidates among the races.

DOE, PNOC fast-track offshore wind infra ahead of clean energy auction. The government moved to resolve regulatory bottlenecks hanging over its nascent offshore wind (OSW) market, securing land and coastal access rights for support infrastructure ahead of the landmark capacity auction. On Aug. 28, the Department of Energy (DOE) and state-run Philippine National Oil Co. (PNOC) signed a memorandum of agreement to acquire tenurial instruments across auxiliary onshore and coastal zones. Under the agreement, the two agencies will secure coastal and land access rights for all upcoming OSW infrastructure prior to the tender. “The partnership strengthens inter-agency collaboration in streamlining project requirements and advancing the country’s offshore wind potential,” PNOC said in a statement. As developers prepare to roll out offshore wind projects, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin highlighted European firms on Thursday as key drivers of the country's clean energy transition. She noted that their expertise in offshore wind, grid modernization, and project financing can convert local energy ambitions into viable, operational developments. “Offshore wind represents a major part of this opportunity, with our upcoming auction targeting 3.3 gigawatts (GW) of capacity,” Garin said. “Beyond electricity generation, offshore wind can mobilize investment across ports, supply chains, engineering, manufacturing, and local employment—areas where European technology, financing, and expertise can play a significant role,” sge added. With tenurial rights secured, the DOE is set to launch the fifth round of the Green Energy Auction (GEA-5) on Dec. 1. The agency expects to issue early contract awards by Dec. 2, with the final bidding phase running through June 30, 2027. The bidding program comes after significant delays. Energy Undersecretary Rowena Guevara previously noted that the recalibrated framework addresses logistical, administrative, and operational bottlenecks. Specifically, it establishes clear administrative structures for environmental fees, performance bonds, monitoring funds, and auxiliary onshore arrangements. The DOE is expected to release formal authorization to proceed with GEA-5 by Oct. 2, alongside finalized guidelines for developers and prospective bidders.

2 women caught in entrapment for robbery with intimidation in Lipa City. CAMP MIGUEL MALVAR, Batangas City — Police arrested two women were arrested in an entrapment operation for alleged robbery with intimidation on Thursday afternoon, Aug. 27 at a convenience store in Bigben Complex, Barangay Mataas na Lupa, Lipa City, Batangas. The Batangas Police Provincial Office (BPPO), director Col. Oliver Ebora identified the suspects as Marjorie, 32, jobless, and Kaye, 28, a laundry attendant, both residents of Lipa City, Batangas. At about 12:15 p.m. Lipa City police conducted operation after a 50-year-old victim filed a complaint that Marjorie was extorting money from him for the supposed settlement of a rape complaint that was earlier filed against him. The victim had previously given the suspects P100,000 after which they allegedly demanded an additional P110,000. According to the victim, the suspects sent him a purported subpoena allegedly issued by the Office of the City Prosecutor of Lipa, indicating that a rape complaint had been filed against him. Upon verification, the subpoena and the purported complaint were found to be fraudulent and non-existent. The suspects also allegedly sent the victim a text message in which the sender misrepresented herself as Police Lt. Col.Aleli Buaquen, Lipa City police chief and instructed him to coordinate and settle the matter amicably. Following the successful completion of the transaction and after the suspects received the marked money from the victim, the operating police immediately effected their arrest. Police recovered the marked money used in the operation , a Settlement Agreement containing the signatures of the victim and one of the suspects, and acellular phone. “We will not tolerate individuals who exploit fear, impersonate government officials, and use fabricated documents to extort money from our citizens, said Ebora. The Batangas PPO remains committed to protecting the public and holding accountable those who abuse the name and authority of the police,” Ebora added. An appropriate charges are being prepared for filing before the Lipa City Prosecutor’s Office.

2,500 people remain in evacuation centers a month after Kumamoto quake. KUMAMOTO (Jiji Press) -- Nearly 2,500 people are still staying in evacuation centers amid scorching heat one month after a powerful earthquake hit the southwestern Japan prefecture of Kumamoto. While efforts toward recovery and reconstruction are underway, challenges remain numerous, with water supply still disrupted in some areas. According to the Kumamoto prefectural government's disaster response headquarters, 38 people were confirmed dead as a result of the July 28 quake, and 33 remained seriously injured, as of 2 p.m. Thursday. Two of the deaths are believed to have been disaster-related, stemming from factors such as heatstroke. The number of evacuees has fallen to 2,460 at 61 shelters in 11 municipalities, down sharply from 10,467 at 415 shelters as of July 30. Each municipality is also working to identify people sheltering at home or in their vehicles through door-to-door visits and other efforts. The 7.1-magnitude earthquake damaged 42,222 houses, including 4,940 that were destroyed or severely damaged and 27,248 that sustained some damage. The extent of damage to 10,034 homes has yet to be determined. The construction of temporary housing has begun, with residents expected to start moving in on Sept. 5. However, water supply disruptions remain a major obstacle to rebuilding lives. Although water supply and sewer service disruptions are expected to be resolved by the end of the month, about 4,400 households in the city of Yatsushiro, where the maximum seismic intensity reached 7, the highest on the Japanese scale, had wells used for daily water supplies damaged. The prefectural government is working with the central government to address the problem, but there is no timetable for a full recovery. Economic damage to businesses and industries totaled about 155.9 billion yen as of Tuesday, while damage to agriculture, forestry and fisheries businesses reached about 110.2 billion yen. Both figures are expected to increase further. A survey found that cancellations at accommodations across the prefecture totaled about 190,000 people, representing roughly 2.7 billion yen in lost revenue. A total of some 140,000 volunteers had taken part in relief efforts across 11 municipalities as of Tuesday. Buses for disaster relief volunteers departing from the city of Kumamoto to the cities of Uki and Yatsushiro and the town of Hikawa, which were devastated by the earthquake, are scheduled to begin operating in stages from Saturday.

Tokyo toy show kicks off. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- More than 180 toy makers are exhibiting new products and flagship items, including those targeting so-called kidults, or adults who enjoy playing with toys, and inbound tourists, as an annual Japanese toy show kicked off in Tokyo on Thursday. Bandai Co. is displaying the Tamagotchi ring, a 2.8-centimeter device that commemorates the 30th anniversary of the debut of its iconic Tamagotchi virtual pet series. It allows users to raise 30 different characters. The company has a section dedicated to the popular manga and anime franchise "Chiikawa." Among the products on display is the Chiikawa Phone Smart, a toy equipped with a camera and apps that allows children to enjoy a realistic smartphone experience. Tomy Co. is exhibiting a model of Plarail railway toys designed after the iconic Doctor Yellow high-speed test train. Its 47-centimeter length allows it to run powerfully on the track. Some toys reflect recent social trends, such as MegaHouse Corp.'s Investment Ranking, a board game in which players grow their wealth by investing in stocks and cryptocurrencies.
